Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB367.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jiguang Huo (寂光豁禪師語錄). Speaker: Jiguang Huo.

Senses.Explanation: To receive the precepts is to undergo their formal conferral. Guxue Zhenzhe says this is no small matter: after reception, the code requires continued dependence on the conferring authorities, and he criticizes recipients who leave after a few hurried days and treat the precept forms like waste paper. Liangshan Yuanguan asks Zhantang Wenzhun whether an unordained novice dares study the Buddha vehicle; Zhantang answers by asking whether the platform, proclamations, pure conduct, or preceptor is the precept. The exchange does not abolish formal reception; it tests where the precept received in that event is located. Konggu Daocheng turns ‘what is called receiving the precepts?’ into a direct public question. Qianshan Shengren Hanke warns that people who refuse reception are like travellers running hazards at midnight, and that receiving and then slighting the precepts is worse. In Bie'an Xingtong's interview, the named participant Shengchu reports ‘receiving the precepts is finished’; Bie'an immediately asks, ‘what precept did you receive?’ An ordination manual preserves the concrete public procedure—head-shaving, the precept master, incense, and spoken formulas—while Jiguang Huo's hall address calls forward those who will receive after defining ‘true precept.’ These records retain the ceremony and also subject its recipient, object, and aftermath to public questioning.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 僧問：「狗子有佛性也無？」師云：「你有佛性也無？」
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB311.xml). Complete Record of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker of this anchored contrast.

Senses.Explanation: The expression is a case-title and saying built from Zhaozhou's recorded answer 'no' when asked whether a dog has buddha-nature. The phrase serves as a title or shorthand for the recorded exchange in which someone asks whether a dog has buddha-nature and Zhaozhou answers 'no.' Dahui's verse heading states 'Zhaozhou: a dog has no buddha-nature' (趙州狗子無佛性) and immediately restates the exchange as 'someone asked about a dog's buddha-nature; Zhaozhou answered, no' (有問狗佛性。趙州答曰無). Other records raise 'the saying that a dog has no buddha-nature' (狗子無佛性話), quote its word 'no' (無字), use it in questioning, and place it beside the separately attested wording 'a dog has buddha-nature' (狗子有佛性). The word 'no' is translated as English 'no.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 觀音在拄杖頭諍論佛法，各持一說，如鬥快龍舟相似。汝諸人為老僧捉下，有功者賞，有過者誅。咦！總是有過，且作麼生誅？」喝一喝，云：「狗銜赦書，諸侯避路。」上堂。「譬如明鏡現眾色像，像不入鏡裏，鏡不到像邊，而森羅宛然，空明自爾。到者裏，須知數點平田白，千株東嶺青，豈不是諸人分上？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianran of Mount Lu (廬山天然禪師語錄). Speaker: Tianran Hanshi.

Senses.Explanation: Tianran Hanshi gives this proverb after staging a dispute among Manjushri, the figure of incisive wisdom; Samantabhadra, the figure of all-encompassing conduct; and Guanyin, the one who attends to cries. He declares all three guilty on the tip of his staff, shouts, and says that a dog carrying a pardon document makes the lords clear the road.
